items.headline: Nvidia's fiscal Q2 revenue hit $96.2 billion (+106% YoY) with EPS of $2.22 beating estimates, and the stock jumped as much as 8.7% Thursday after guidance implied 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028 and customer compute commitments jumped from $119 billion to $279 billion in a single quarter
items.why: A beat and forward-commitment jump this size resets the ceiling for the AI-hardware trade heading into a week when a hawkish Fed speech could otherwise have dominated sentiment.

items.headline: AMD posted Q2 2026 EPS of $1.66, beating estimates of $1.55 by 7.1%, with revenue of $21.3 billion driven by strong MI350 data-center GPU shipments, while trading at a 27-28x forward multiple versus Nvidia's premium valuation
items.why: AMD's execution on MI350 is the clearest evidence yet that hyperscalers are actively diversifying away from single-vendor AI chip dependence, not just talking about it.

items.headline: Salesforce shares surged 22.6% after crushing estimates with $5.90 EPS against a $3.27 forecast and $11.35 billion in revenue, while Nvidia's earnings halo lifted Broadcom 4.5% and Intel 4.4% in the same session
items.why: A software company's earnings beat driving a bigger single-day pop than most chipmakers shows how much of this rally is now about confirmation of AI monetization broadly, not just GPU sales.

items.headline: The SEC proposed 'Regulation Crypto Assets' on Aug. 18, its first tailored securities-offering regime for crypto: a one-time $5 million exemption over four years, a $75 million annual exemption with reporting requirements, and a conditional safe harbor from the 'investment contract' definition
items.why: A dedicated offering framework, rather than enforcement-by-lawsuit, changes the calculus for crypto projects deciding whether to raise capital onshore or offshore.

items.headline: US spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs pulled in a combined $2.6 billion through Aug. 21 -- the strongest inflow week in about 10 months -- as Bitcoin surged toward $80,000 following the Treasury's Aug. 19 bond-buyback expansion and a White House meeting where Trump floated the idea of the US accumulating Bitcoin
items.why: ETF inflows arriving alongside falling yields and White House signaling suggests this rally is drawing genuine new capital rather than just short covering, though one strong week doesn't establish a trend.

items.headline: Bitcoin briefly touched $81,455 overnight Friday -- its highest level since May 15 -- before pulling back to around $79,850 as traders positioned ahead of Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech; $82,800 is the key resistance level where BTC was rejected in May ahead of a slide to $57,000
items.why: That $82,800 level carries real memory for traders -- a clean break above it opens genuine price discovery, while another rejection there risks reviving the pattern that preceded this year's steepest drawdown.

items.headline: In his first Jackson Hole speech as Fed Chair, Kevin Warsh said recent inflation data 'do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved' and that the Fed will 'have work to do' if confidence in the 2% target doesn't return, while pointedly criticizing the Treasury's bond-buyback expansion as the kind of 'unconventional policy' that 'should be used sparingly, if at all'
items.why: A Fed chair publicly pushing back on his own Treasury Secretary's market intervention is a rare institutional friction point -- it signals the Fed-Treasury coordination markets leaned on all August may not hold.

sources.title: Rate-hike expectations rise on Warsh speech at Jackson Hole
Gold price drops as Warsh warns Fed still has 'work to do' on inflation

items.headline: September rate-hike odds jumped to 46% from 35% the prior day after Warsh's remarks, per CME data, while the 2-year Treasury yield rose 6.6 basis points to 4.29% (a one-month high) even as the 30-year eased 3 basis points to 5.16%
items.why: The short end selling off while the long end barely moves is the market pricing near-term hike risk without losing confidence in the Fed's longer-run inflation fight -- a more contained reaction than the speech's tone might suggest.

sources.title: Rate-hike expectations rise on Warsh speech at Jackson Hole

items.headline: Heading into the speech, Treasury yields were already at multi-year highs -- the 10-year near 4.71% and the 30-year at 5.33%, a level not seen in nearly two decades -- amid persistent above-target inflation and a federal debt load exceeding $40 trillion
items.why: Yields this elevated before a hawkish-leaning speech even landed shows the bond market had already priced in a chunk of the 'higher for longer' story Warsh went on to confirm.

sources.title: Treasury Yields and Stock Market Impact: Your August 2026 Investment Guide

items.headline: Oil fell below $83 a barrel, down roughly 5% on the week, after Iran and Oman agreed a revenue-sharing framework for the Strait of Hormuz and Goldman Sachs estimated Gulf oil exports have recovered to 15-16 million barrels a day -- about two-thirds of pre-conflict levels -- even as Washington told mediators it won't revive the collapsed June ceasefire terms
items.why: Markets are now pricing the Iran standoff as a sanctions-and-diplomacy story rather than a physical-supply threat, which is exactly the kind of reassessment that can unwind an oil risk premium fast if it holds.

sources.title: Oil Heads for Weekly Loss

items.headline: Gold tumbled as much as 3.2% to $4,515.30 an ounce after Warsh's hawkish-leaning remarks and his pointed criticism of the Treasury bond-buyback 'debasement trade' that had powered gold's best month since January; bullion is still up about 11% in August but remains 16% below its late-January record
items.why: Gold giving back a chunk of its Warsh-speech gains on the same day the Fed chair criticized the exact policy that drove the rally shows how much of August's move was policy-dependent rather than purely safe-haven demand.

sources.title: Gold price drops as Warsh warns Fed still has 'work to do' on inflation

items.headline: Comex copper set a fresh record at $6.727 a pound, topping the previous record of $6.714 set Aug. 12, as the threat of US import tariffs (15% from 2027, stepping to 30% from 2028) keeps pulling metal into American warehouses and turns a projected 639,000-tonne global surplus into what analysts call a de facto deficit
items.why: A market flipping from surplus to scarcity purely on anticipated tariffs, before any duty is actually enacted, shows how much of today's copper price is a bet on Washington rather than physical demand.

items.headline: Oil fell below $83 a barrel, extending its weekly loss to near 5%, as an Iran-Oman revenue-sharing deal over the Strait of Hormuz and recovering Gulf export volumes (15-16 million barrels a day) further eased the supply-risk premium
items.why: Crude giving back its geopolitical risk premium this fast suggests traders think the worst-case Hormuz scenario is now off the table, at least until the next escalation.

items.why: An RSI this extended paired with a fresh breakout is the kind of setup that either grinds higher on momentum or snaps back hard -- there's little room left for a gentle consolidation.

items.headline: The Treasury curve bear-flattened post-Warsh: the 2-year yield jumped 6.6 basis points to 4.29% (a one-month high) while the 30-year eased 3 basis points to 5.16% and the 10-year held flat at 4.672%
items.why: Short rates rising while long rates hold steady or fall is the bond market's way of saying it believes the Fed can hike without reigniting long-run inflation expectations -- a vote of confidence that could evaporate fast if the next CPI print disagrees.
